title: The limit shape and emergence of the Discrete Gaussian level lines
summary: Consider the $(2+1)$D Discrete Gaussian model (ZGFF) on an $L\times L$ box with a hard floor at height zero and zero boundary conditions, at low temperature. The second author, Martinelli and Sly (2016) showed that the surface has a plateau, filling nearly the full square, at height either $H$ or $H+1$ for an explicit function $H(L)$. In a companion paper, we studied the local laws of the top level lines near the four sides of the box, and showed that after rescaling each by $(L^{2/3-o(1)},L^{1/3-o(1)})$, they converge to a product of Ferrari--Spohn diffusions.
